p: Tukoji was born on 26 November 1890, the son of Shivajirao Holkar, Maharaja of Indore, and Maharani Sita Bai. His father abdicated on 31 January 1903, and as the new maharaja was only thirteen a council of regency governed until he came of age. He was educated at the Daly College in Indore and at Dehradun. On 6 November 1911 he was invested with ruling powers, and in the same year he attended the coronation of King George V in London.

As ruler he founded two orders, the Order of Merit of Holkar in February 1914 and the Order of Ahilyabai Holkar on 22 November 1920. In the New Year Honours of 1918 he was made a Knight Grand Commander of the Order of the Star of India.

In January 1925 Mumtaz Begum, a courtesan and one of his mistresses, left his harem after what she described as repressive conditions and the death of her daughter, which she blamed on palace nurses. While performing in Bombay she met Abdul Bawla, a 25-year-old Memon businessman, who was threatened several times and told to send her back, and refused. On 12 January a group of assassins attacked the couple at Malabar Hill. Bawla was shot in the head and killed; Mumtaz Begum survived with a wound to the face after British officers who were nearby intervened.

She testified against nine accused, among them men of the maharaja's household. The court sentenced three men to death and three to life imprisonment. One of the latter, General Anandrao Gangram Phanse of the Indore army, escaped the death penalty after being represented by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The court did not formally hold Tukoji responsible, but under British pressure he abdicated on 26 February 1926 and left Indore.

After his abdication he lived mainly in France. He had married three times. His senior wife, Chandravati Gawade, whom he married on 16 March 1895 when both were small children, stayed in Indore and brought up their son, the new maharaja. His second wife, Indira Talcherkar, married in 1913, also remained there and became a patron of historical research bodies such as the Rajwade Historical Research Institute.

In 1928 he married Nancy Anne Miller, who before the wedding embraced Hinduism, was received into the Dhangar community and took the name Sharmista Devi Holkar; they had four daughters. The Bawla case inspired a film of 1925, Kulin Kanta, and two books. Tukoji died in Paris on 21 May 1978, leaving one son and six daughters.

notes: The article gives the attack as 'January 12' following 'In January 1925' for the escape; it does not make clear that escape and murder fell in the same month (the escape must have been earlier). I wrote 'In January 1925 ... left his harem' and 'On 12 January' as the article does, without adding a year to the second. Please check: the murder is 12 January 1925, so the escape date in the article is probably loose.
The article says Bombay once and Mumbai once; I used Bombay as the existing description does.
'ICC, Dehradun' in the article: I wrote only 'at Dehradun'.
The existing description credits him with cotton trade and public works; the article says nothing of either.
